title: Heirs of Spouses Liwagon v. Heirs of Spouses Liwagon
summary: The Supreme Court ruled on the effect of preterition (total omission of a compulsory heir in the will). Preterition annuls the institution of heir but does not affect devises and legacies insofar as they are not inofficious or excessive.
doctrine: Preterition or the total omission of a compulsory heir from the will annuls the institution of heir under Article 854 of the Civil Code. However, devises and legacies shall be valid insofar as they are not inofficious. The omitted heir is entitled to his legitime.
fullText:
BRION, J.:

The issue is the effect of preterition on the testamentary dispositions in the decedent's will.

Article 854 of the Civil Code provides that the preterition or omission of one, some, or all of the compulsory heirs in the direct line, whether living at the time of the execution of the will or born after the death of the testator, shall annul the institution of heir.

Preterition consists in the silence of the testator with regard to a compulsory heir, omitting him in the will. It differs from disinheritance in that preterition is merely an omission without an express exclusion.
